title: Extract a multi-line filter lambda into a named predicate

blocks.text: When a filter lambda grows several conditions long, the page suggests giving it a name: a `Predicate<User> isEligible` reads better in the stream than a block of `&&` checks, and it can be tested on its own.
`User` is given, nested in `Eligibility`: `record User(String name, int age, boolean active, boolean verifiedEmail)`. Write two static methods:

items: `isEligible()` returns a `Predicate<User>` that is true for a user who is active, at least 18 years old, and has a verified email.
`eligibleNames(List<User> users)` returns the names of the eligible users in alphabetical order, using that predicate.

blocks.text: Mind the exact age limit, and every one of the three conditions.

cases.says: Only active adults with a verified email are kept, their names in alphabetical order.
A user who is exactly 18 counts as an adult.
An active adult whose email is not verified is not eligible.

concepts: A lambda that grows several conditions long reads better as a named predicate or method.
